principles: Ideas have the highest content leverage: topic (what you talk about) + angle (your take) + substance (facts, opinions, examples supporting it).
Select topics FIRST from actual content-performance data. Prioritize topics gaining traction in the most recent 7–21 days; publication recency or news coverage alone is not trend validation.

Use validated topics that have worked before. Then mine Andrew’s daily context for a NEW, nonobvious take and tactically implementable substance. Do not use daily-work anecdotes as a substitute for demonstrated audience interest.

Audience direction under consideration: established coaching, education, founder/creator-led businesses in the info/online-marketing space, including eight- and nine-figure businesses; this audience fit is not verified by broad-AI engagement.
Content fails either through topic alignment (the viewer does not care) or take/substance (boring, generic, inapplicable). Evaluate these separately.
Read what the successful source already says before proposing a new angle. The source’s existing insight is not Andrew’s original contribution.
Operating loop: recent performance evidence → buyer relevance → source’s existing take → Andrew’s distinct contribution → concrete action/demo → measure qualified response and business relevance.
Keep original evidence and metrics separate from proposals and outcomes. Use Outlier Lab as the durable input/output home; archive selected examples independently of the rolling feed.
caveats: Initial screen: Sandcastles existing tracked creators, last 21 days, reported outlier ≥3×, views ≥50K, engagement ≥2%; 21 accepted results. Thresholds are a discovery screen, not a universal validation rule.
Sandcastles scores have not been independently recalculated. Do not combine them with Outlier Lab’s plays/account-median formula.
No longitudinal velocity measurements or multi-creator topic cluster validation have been completed for these selections. Status is performance-backed candidate, not proven emerging trend.
Direct Instagram links and creator identity were checked. Where age displays conflict, the original post timestamp is retained separately. Comment-to-DM requests may contribute to engagement.
No private client data, paid scraping, new recurring refresh, or social publication is included in this import.

items.topic: Finding where AI should actually be used in a business
items.creator: @heystevetan
items.sourceCaption: Asking your team "where could we use AI?" gets you nothing useful. They aren’t AI experts. They’re experts in their own work, which is a completely different question.

metrics.source: Sandcastles tracked-channel library; displayed rounded values

items.status: Performance-backed candidate · audience fit to test
items.audienceFit: Strong conceptual fit for established founders choosing AI implementation priorities; viewers’ company size and buying intent are unverified.
items.sourceTake: The caption presents Codos and employee interviews as a way to discover actual workflows before selecting technology. Those are the creator’s/product’s claims, not independently verified delivery results.
items.proposedTake: The task employees complain about most is not necessarily the bottleneck worth automating. Examine work that repeatedly returns to the founder for judgment.
substance: Proposed diagnostic: review a consent-appropriate week of approval requests and classify missing information, unclear decision rules, and decisions genuinely requiring founder judgment.
Show one example where better access to information helps, one where a clear decision rule is needed, and one where human judgment remains appropriate.
Measure founder escalations and rework before and after any pilot. Do not claim saved time or ROI before measurement.
The original comments inspected include discussion of diagnosing before building, plus many Codos keyword requests. These show interaction, not verified buyer qualification.
items.evidenceLimit: Single-post outperformance is not proof of an accelerating topic-wide trend, organic reach, buyer revenue level, or causal topic effect. Proposed angles are editorial hypotheses, not measured business outcomes. Novelty has not been exhaustively established. Sandcastles age and Instagram’s original timestamp differ; exact Instagram timestamp is recorded. Full video was not audiovisually reviewed.

items.topic: Rebuilding useful software features with AI
items.creator: @theaisurfer
items.sourceCaption: You can point an agent at any app you love and have it rebuild the exact feature you want, no source code needed.

metrics.source: Sandcastles tracked-channel library; displayed rounded values

items.audienceFit: Relevant to founders evaluating custom internal tools or replacing narrowly used software features. Broad builder attention is not proof of eight-figure-founder demand.
items.sourceTake: The caption promotes Reverse Engineer Anything and claims an agent can inspect and recreate app features without source code. Exact equivalence, speed and success are source claims.
items.proposedTake: Before replacing a subscription with an AI-built tool, test the things the demo never shows: revisions, exports, failures, and recovering your work.
substance: Andrew’s Oct 25 REA investigation established its software/runtime focus and explored adapting its evidence method; it did not prove a working video-editing pipeline.
Proposed demo: choose one permitted feature, then test normal use, revision, usable export, missing input, and recovery after failure.
Keep observed behavior separate from inferred implementation; document which functions remain unsupported.
Use only software/features and materials you have permission to inspect and recreate; do not copy proprietary code/assets or bypass licensing.

items.topic: Reactivating dormant customers instead of only buying new traffic
items.creator: @neilpatel with @gohighlevel
items.sourceCaption: It’s not a new ad campaign. It’s the list of customers who haven’t been back in six months. One message to all of them. Almost nobody sends it.

metrics.source: Sandcastles tracked-channel library; displayed rounded values

items.audienceFit: Relevant to coaching, education and established customer businesses with appropriate contact permission. Adapt the example to former students/clients rather than assume ecommerce-only fit.
items.sourceTake: The caption recommends contacting dormant customers and claims the existing list is a cheap revenue opportunity. The original Instagram post displays both Neil Patel and GoHighLevel.
items.proposedTake: Six months of silence does not explain why someone stopped buying. Someone who succeeded, someone who got stuck, and someone who had a bad experience should not receive the same comeback message.
substance: Proposed demo: classify a small consent-appropriate sample using purchase and support history; retain an unknown category instead of inferring motives.
Show different follow-up routes for satisfied graduates, stalled customers and unresolved complaints; human review for sensitive cases.
Suppress unsubscribed/do-not-contact records and respect channel-specific consent.
Measure replies, reactivation and complaints against a comparable baseline or holdout before asserting lift.
items.evidenceLimit: Single-post outperformance is not proof of an accelerating topic-wide trend, organic reach, buyer revenue level, or causal topic effect. Proposed angles are editorial hypotheses, not measured business outcomes. Novelty has not been exhaustively established. Collaboration authorship means the reported Sandcastles score is not an independently verified personal-account baseline. No reactivation campaign or revenue result is claimed.

items.creator: @tenfoldmarc
items.sourceCaption: If you want to get these just comment "studio" and I’ll send you an invite link. Spoken transcript begins: "Claude, can you make all of these effects?"

metrics.source: Existing Outlier Lab cached reel data and rendered ratio; data build 2026-10-26

items.status: Existing reel enriched · proposed implementation lesson
items.audienceFit: Useful for founders with a content team seeking repeatable production. Comment-based resource demand does not establish buyer intent or editing quality.
items.sourceTake: The cached TokScript transcript lists effects and invites a studio keyword comment to access a set of 46 effects. The transcript is machine generated.
items.proposedTake: An effects library is not a repeatable content workflow. Prove one complete edit from raw footage through revision and usable export before scaling production.
substance: Andrew’s recent editing work distinguishes working components, an unfinished preview, a review handoff and an accepted deliverable. Do not present the unfinished work as a successful case study.
Proposed test: take one permissioned raw clip, produce an edit, request a concrete revision, and inspect the final export.
Track correction time and quality failures as well as generation speed; a picker demo is not proof a client video is finished.
